item.text:
**6B.5 Research Note: Narendra Modi in 2024**

**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning positive on administrative measurement and grievance redress, but only partly supported on transparent correction. The strongest evidence is official self-reporting on CPGRAMS, AI-assisted grievance handling, and digital delivery systems; the clearest counterevidence is that correction was uneven in practice, especially for poor children and when budget choices were shaped by coalition bargaining.

**Accepted claims**
- [CPGRAMS: 3 Years, 70 Lakh Grievances Solved](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2088830&lang=2&reg=3) — Press Information Bureau, 30 Dec 2024. Claim: the government framed service delivery as “last mile” citizen-centric governance and said CPGRAMS had solved 70 lakh grievances, indicating heavy reliance on measured complaint resolution. QIDs: 6B.5; 6B.4
- [Union Government issues Comprehensive Guidelines for Handling Public Grievances](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2048939&lang=2&reg=48) — Press Information Bureau, 26 Aug 2024. Claim: the government formalized time-bound grievance handling, escalation, SMS/email feedback, AI-powered analytics, and a monthly grievance index, which is direct evidence of measurement and correction mechanisms. QIDs: 6B.5; 6B.4
- [PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ENHANCING COMPLAINT REDRESSAL THROUGH CPGRAM](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2083263) — Press Information Bureau, 11 Dec 2024. Claim: the government reported 1.12 crore grievances redressed since 2020, 13-day average disposal in 2024, and root-cause analysis, which is strong evidence of process monitoring and iterative correction. QIDs: 6B.5; 6B.4
- [With renewed focus on next generation administrative reforms](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1997326&lang=2&reg=48) — Press Information Bureau, 18 Jan 2024. Claim: Modi’s government approved funding for AI-assisted CPGRAMS plus process re-engineering and “seamless service delivery up to the last mile,” showing explicit investment in administrative capacity. QIDs: 6B.5; 6B.4
- [Update on Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2081482&lang=2&reg=48) — Press Information Bureau, 6 Dec 2024. Claim: ABDM expanded ABHA, facility registries, professional registries, and linked health records at scale, which is evidence of measurement-heavy service delivery infrastructure. QIDs: 6B.5; 6B.4
- [India’s finance minister unveils budget with focus on poor, women, youth and farmers](https://theprint.in/india/indias-finance-minister-unveils-budget-with-focus-on-poor-women-youth-and-farmers/1948406/) — Reuters via ThePrint, 1 Feb 2024. Claim: the interim budget publicly centered disadvantaged groups and avoided a classic giveaway, a weak but real signal that social spending was routed through budgetary planning rather than pure patronage. QIDs: 6B.5; 6B.4; 6B.3
- [India’s Modi spends billions on jobs, key allies in first budget after election](https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-spends-billions-on-jobs-key-allies-in-first-budget-after-election/2187546/) — Reuters via ThePrint, 23 Jul 2024. Claim: the post-election budget explicitly aimed to win back voters and retain coalition support, including over $5 billion for coalition-led states, which weakens the case for neutral, evidence-based correction. QIDs: 6B.5; 6B.4
- [India’s high food inflation leaves less in lunch boxes of poor school children](https://theprint.in/india/indias-high-food-inflation-leaves-less-in-lunch-boxes-of-poor-school-children/2307077/) — Reuters via ThePrint, 11 Oct 2024. Claim: school meal budgets had not kept pace with food inflation, forcing cutbacks for poor children, which is direct counterevidence that service delivery was being corrected quickly enough for vulnerable users. QIDs: 6B.5; 6B.3

**Search gap**
- I found strong official evidence that Modi’s government built measurement and grievance machinery, but very little independent auditing that these tools materially improved frontline services in 2024.
- The best positive claims are mostly government self-reports; the best negative claims are outcome-based distress signals or patronage-driven budget coverage, not direct audits of delivery quality.
- I did not find strong independent evidence on sanitation, local health clinics, PDS, or school administration reforms beyond the digital/grievance and school-meal material above.
